newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's April industrial activity up 15.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's April industrial activity up 15.0 pct.

text.p: Mexico's overall industrial activity in April grew 15.0 percent compared with the same month in 1996, partly fueled by a 16.3 percent increase in manufacturing and a 15.4 percent rise in construction, the Finance Ministry said on Tuesday.
In a Reuters survey, analysts had on average expected a rise of 7.92 percent in industrial activity.

The Finance Ministry said the figure was higher than expected due to the fact that Easter fell during April of last year and this year fell during March. This means that April 1997 had more working days than April 1996.
Factoring out the extra days this April, industrial production would have risen about 8 percent, the ministry said.
Mining was up 5.8 percent from April 1996, the Finance Ministry said, while generation of electricity, gas and water grew 6.1 percent.
During the first four months of the year, industrial activity rose 8.4 percent compared to the same period of last year, the ministry said.

During that time, mining grew 2.3 percent versus the first four months of last year, while manufacturing grew 8.7 percent. Within manufacturing, non-maquiladora sector manufactures grew 8.4 percent and maquiladora manufactures grew 13.2 percent.
Construction grew 10.4 percent during the year's first four months versus the same period of 1996. Generation of electricity and gas grew 5.6 percent during that period.
